# Looms

The commands `mt help` lists under Looms. Memory is known as looms in Maitento, which is why these commands start with `loom-`. More in [Memory](../../../concepts/memory.md).

In a terminal, type `mt` and then the command. In the interactive shell and the cloud shell, type the command on
its own. `mt help <command>` shows the same details in your terminal.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`loom-create`](#loom-create) | Create a loom in a namespace |
| [`loom-cut`](#loom-cut) | Let a thread go: its words are released, and a knot keeps its essence and why it was let go |
| [`loom-delete`](#loom-delete) | Erase (unravel) a loom and every thread, tension, panel, pattern, session and night weaving in it (tenant admins only) |
| [`loom-give`](#loom-give) | Give a thread to another loom: it arrives second-hand, saying where it came from (only shared knowledge travels) |
| [`loom-inspect`](#loom-inspect) | Inspect a loom: its shape, what is held close, what is fraying, tensions and the last night weaving |
| [`loom-list`](#loom-list) | List the looms in a namespace |
| [`loom-night-spend`](#loom-night-spend) | Show the night weavings of every loom in the tenant since a moment, with what each one spent |
| [`loom-night-weave`](#loom-night-weave) | Ask for a loom to be night-woven now, without waiting for the quiet period |
| [`loom-panels`](#loom-panels) | Show a loom's panels: the portrait in prose night weaving writes of each person or thing the loom knows |
| [`loom-pattern`](#loom-pattern) | Show the pattern a loom keeps of a codebase, or shape it (how it is built, how to find your way, where to start, its conventions) |
| [`loom-pattern-delete`](#loom-pattern-delete) | Erase the whole pattern a loom keeps of a codebase; to drop one item, use loom-pattern `--remove` (tenant admins only) |
| [`loom-patterns`](#loom-patterns) | List the patterns a loom keeps: the shape of each codebase its agents work in, and when each last changed |
| [`loom-pin`](#loom-pin) | Hold a thread close, so it is in every future tapestry, or release it with `--release` |
| [`loom-recall`](#loom-recall) | Recall the threads that matter for a question, most relevant first (looking does not strengthen them) |
| [`loom-reflect`](#loom-reflect) | Show everything a loom holds about a topic (foundations, what was woven across them, tensions, what was let go, and how understanding moved) |
| [`loom-reframe`](#loom-reframe) | Reframe a thread with new wording, weight or foundational status; a seam keeps what it was and why it changed |
| [`loom-seed`](#loom-seed) | Seed a loom from another: copy in the strongest of its shared knowledge, each thread marked as inherited |
| [`loom-sessions`](#loom-sessions) | List agents' recent sessions with a loom (who, in which interaction run, when, and whether night weaving has consolidated them) |
| [`loom-tapestry`](#loom-tapestry) | Show what an agent would wake up knowing: the tapestry woven for the people present |
| [`loom-tension-resolve`](#loom-tension-resolve) | Resolve an open tension, saying how: the loom keeps the resolution, and neither thread is changed |
| [`loom-tensions`](#loom-tensions) | Show a loom's open tensions, threads pulling against each other (`--all` includes resolved ones) |
| [`loom-thread`](#loom-thread) | Show one thread in full: what it says, its standing, where it came from, how it changed, and how it has been used |
| [`loom-threads`](#loom-threads) | List a loom's threads, filtered and sorted as you choose (by default newest first, without knots) |
| [`loom-unravel-thread`](#loom-unravel-thread) | Erase (unravel) one thread, with any tension and panel derived from it, for data-subject erasure; to let a thread go and keep a knot, use loom-cut (tenant admins only) |
| [`loom-update`](#loom-update) | Rename a loom, or change its description or night-weaving settings (only what you give changes) |
| [`loom-weave`](#loom-weave) | Weave a thread into a loom (a near-duplicate reinforces the existing thread instead) |
| [`loom-weavings`](#loom-weavings) | Show a loom's night weavings: what each night consolidated, and the dream log it wrote |

## loom-create

Create a loom in a namespace.

```text
mt loom-create <name> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | text | yes |  | The loom's name (3-250 characters, unique in the namespace) |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--description, -d <value>` | text |  |  | What the loom is for |
| `--night-weaving <value>` | text |  |  | true or false: consolidate the loom once its sessions go quiet (default: true) |
| `--quiet-minutes <number>` | whole number |  |  | Minutes of quiet before night weaving may begin, 1-1440 (default: 15) |
| `--weaver-model <value>` | text |  |  | The model night weaving thinks with (default: the bound agent's own) |

## loom-cut

Let a thread go: its words are released, and a knot keeps its essence and why it was let go.

```text
mt loom-cut <thread> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<thread>` | text | yes |  | The thread: its full id or the short id loom-threads shows |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--acknowledgment, -a <value>` | text | yes |  | Why it is being let go |
| `--essence, -e <value>` | text |  |  | What is worth keeping, in the knot; leave it out to let the thread go entirely |

## loom-delete

Erase (unravel) a loom and every thread, tension, panel, pattern, session and night weaving in it (tenant admins only).

```text
mt loom-delete [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--confirm` | flag |  |  | Confirm the erasure; without it, the command only says what would go (there is no undo) |


|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<thread>` | text | yes |  | The thread to give: its full id or the short id loom-threads shows |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--to <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom to give it to: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--note, -n <value>` | text |  |  | What to say with it (kept with the gift) |

## loom-night-spend

Show the night weavings of every loom in the tenant since a moment, with what each one spent.

```text
mt loom-night-spend [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--since <value>` | text |  |  | From this moment, in ISO 8601, UTC unless an offset is given (default: 24 hours ago) |
| `--limit <number>` | whole number |  | `20` | At most this many nights, newest first (1-200) |

## loom-pattern

Show the pattern a loom keeps of a codebase, or shape it (how it is built, how to find your way, where to start, its conventions).

```text
mt loom-pattern <codebase> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<codebase>` | text | yes |  | The codebase's name, for example billing-api |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--architecture <value>` | text |  |  | Replace the summary of how it is built with this: a few sentences about its shape |
| `--heuristic <value>` | text |  |  | Add one way to find your way around it, in a line |
| `--key-file <value>` | text |  |  | Add one file or folder worth starting from, and why if it helps |
| `--convention <value>` | text |  |  | Add one convention it keeps, in a line |
| `--remove <value>` | text |  |  | Drop items that are no longer true, from any list: those whose text starts with this, in any case |
| `--width <number>` | whole number |  |  | Line width in characters (default: the terminal's) |

## loom-pattern-delete

Erase the whole pattern a loom keeps of a codebase; to drop one item, use loom-pattern `--remove` (tenant admins only).

```text
mt loom-pattern-delete <codebase> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<codebase>` | text | yes |  | The name of the codebase whose pattern to erase |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--confirm` | flag |  |  | Confirm the erasure; without it, the command only shows what would go (there is no undo) |
| `--width <number>` | whole number |  |  | Line width in characters, for showing what would go (default: the terminal's) |

## loom-pin

Hold a thread close, so it is in every future tapestry, or release it with `--release`.

```text
mt loom-pin <thread> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<thread>` | text | yes |  | The thread: its full id or the short id loom-threads shows |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--release` | flag |  |  | Release the thread instead: it goes back to being woven into a tapestry only when it matters |

## loom-recall

Recall the threads that matter for a question, most relevant first (looking does not strengthen them).

```text
mt loom-recall <query> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<query>` | text | yes |  | A question, a topic or a name |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--limit <number>` | whole number |  | `8` | At most this many threads (1-50) |
| `--kind, -k <value>` | text |  |  | Only these kinds, comma-separated: semantic, episodic, relational, procedural, reflection, intention |
| `--about, -a <value>` | text |  |  | Who is present, comma-separated: threads about them rank higher |
| `--recency <number>` | number |  |  | How much to favour recently used threads, 0 to 1: 0 ranks on salience alone (default: 0.2) |

## loom-reframe

Reframe a thread with new wording, weight or foundational status; a seam keeps what it was and why it changed.

```text
mt loom-reframe <thread> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<thread>` | text | yes |  | The thread: its full id or the short id loom-threads shows |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--reason, -r <value>` | text | yes |  | Why it is being reframed (the seam keeps it) |
| `--content, -c <value>` | text |  |  | The new wording |
| `--weight, -w <number>` | number |  |  | The new weight, 0 to 1 |
| `--foundational <value>` | text |  |  | true makes it warp (a foundation, which never frays); false makes it weft |
| `--acknowledgment <value>` | text |  |  | Needed to revise a foundation (a warp thread): say plainly that you are renegotiating it |
| `--remind-when <value>` | text |  |  | Replace the words that bring it back, comma-separated; "none" clears them |

## loom-threads

List a loom's threads, filtered and sorted as you choose (by default newest first, without knots).

```text
mt loom-threads [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--kind, -k <value>` | text |  |  | Only these kinds, comma-separated: semantic, episodic, relational, procedural, reflection, intention |
| `--strand <value>` | text |  |  | Only this strand: warp (foundations) or weft |
| `--knots <value>` | text |  |  | Threads let go (knots): exclude, include or only (default: exclude) |
| `--pinned <value>` | text |  |  | true: only threads held close; false: only the rest |
| `--subject, -s <value>` | text |  |  | Only threads about this subject |
| `--tag, -t <value>` | text |  |  | Only threads carrying this tag (`--tag` theme lists night weaving's themes) |
| `--visibility <value>` | text |  |  | Only shared or only private threads: shared or private |
| `--sort <value>` | text |  |  | Order: newest, weight, recently-accessed or most-frayed (default: newest) |
| `--skip <number>` | whole number |  |  | Skip this many threads first, to page through them (at most 10000) |
| `--limit <number>` | whole number |  | `50` | At most this many threads (1-500) |

```text
mt loom-update [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |

| `--clear <value>` | text |  |  | Return these to their defaults, comma-separated: description, night-weaving, quiet-minutes, weaver-model |

## loom-weave

Weave a thread into a loom (a near-duplicate reinforces the existing thread instead).

```text
mt loom-weave <content> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<content>` | text | yes |  | What to remember |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--kind, -k <value>` | text |  |  | semantic, episodic, relational, procedural, reflection, or intention: something to do when its moment comes, which needs `--remind-when` (default: semantic) |
| `--weight, -w <number>` | number |  |  | How much it matters, 0 to 1 |
| `--about, -a <value>` | text |  |  | Who or what it is about, comma-separated |
| `--tags, -t <value>` | text |  |  | Tags, comma-separated |
| `--foundational <value>` | text |  |  | true makes it warp (a foundation, which never frays); false forces weft (default: warp only for relational threads) |
| `--decay <value>` | text |  |  | How fast it fades unused: never, slow, normal or fast (warp never fades) |
| `--private` | flag |  |  | Mark it private: only the agent that wove a private thread sees it, so one woven from the shell reaches no agent |
| `--pin` | flag |  |  | Hold it close, so it is in every future tapestry |
| `--remind-when <value>` | text |  |  | Words that bring it back to the agent when someone says them, comma-separated |
| `--replaces <value>` | text |  |  | A thread this corrects or replaces, by full or short id: that thread is let go, keeping what it said |
| `--until <value>` | text |  |  | When it stops holding, as YYYY-MM-DD: after that day it is no longer offered |
| `--basis <value>` | text |  |  | What it rests on: said, impression (a reading nobody said) or read, from a document or tool (default: said) |

## loom-weavings

Show a loom's night weavings: what each night consolidated, and the dream log it wrote.

```text
mt loom-weavings [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--loom, -l <value>` | text | yes |  | The loom: its id, or its name in the namespace |
| `--limit <number>` | whole number |  | `10` | At most this many nights, newest first (1-200) |
